source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's DFW2 campus in Lewisville publishes 12 MW of IT capacity across 200,000 square feet of technical space, and that is the whole of the published power figure.

The spec page does not state a rack count, an accelerator count, a power usage effectiveness, or a tenant roster. Any conversion to racks or GPUs is an outside assumption, not an operator fact. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 12 MW of IT load is roughly 300 racks. At 10 kW per rack, the same load is roughly 1,200 racks. The arithmetic is an assumption about density, not a fact about this building.

The certifications qualify the campus for specific workloads rather than describing who occupies it. PCI DSS covers payment card data, HIPAA covers protected health information, ISO 27001 covers an information security management system, FISMA covers federal information systems, SSAE 16 Type II covers controls relevant to financial reporting, and TIA-942 covers telecommunications infrastructure design. None of these names a tenant, and the operator does not publish one here.

Texas holds 137 mapped facilities, of which 19 publish a megawatt figure this site has read. Those 19 total 475.41 MW, and DFW2 ranks twelfth among them by published capacity. The ranking is therefore a ranking within a minority of Texas facilities, since most mapped sites publish no figure at all. On the published numbers, this is a mid-sized campus in the largest concentration of data centers this site maps, and its 12 MW is a small share of the state's published total.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
